name: German Air Quality Index (Umweltbundesamt Luftqualitätsindex)
version: 2025 risk-based revision (live on UBA API v4)

sources.title: UBA, Umwelt und Gesundheit 08/2025: Überarbeitung des Luftqualitätsindex nach den WHO-Leitlinien 2021, Table 5 'Proposal 2 for risk-based AQI'
Empirical confirmation: 129,519 station-hours of UBA Air Data API v4 /airquality output (2026-01, 2026-07, 2026-10). Every observed band edge matches Proposal 2.

categories.label: Good
categories.health: Enjoy outdoor activities; health effects are unlikely.

categories.label: Moderate
categories.health: Short-term effects are unlikely, but long-term exposure at this level can harm health. Sensitive people may want to limit strenuous outdoor activity.

categories.label: Poor
categories.health: Sensitive groups should avoid strenuous outdoor activity. Others should reduce it if symptoms appear.

categories.label: Very poor
categories.health: Health effects possible for everyone. Postpone strenuous outdoor activity or move it to a place with better air.

rules: Each pollutant's hourly mean, rounded half-up to an integer, is classified into 5 bands with inclusive upper bounds. The index is the worst class (UBA: 'the pollutant with the worst index value determines the overall index').
An index is formed as soon as one pollutant is available (UBA report, section on application to 2019/2022 data).
notes: UBA's 2023 documentation (lqi_dokumentation_final_202305.pdf) describes the previous index (NO2 0-20 'very good', PM as a 24-h mean). The API no longer uses it. The live classification matches the 2025 risk-based proposal exactly, including SO2.

Colours are AirAtlas's palette. UBA's official colours could not be verified because the UBA website was in maintenance mode on 2026-10-21. Health texts are short paraphrases of the 2025 report's Table 6 recommendations.
